automate_and_routing.automate: Agents at work polls /api/runs every 4 seconds for worker, schedule and session rows. Only scheduled runs expose Stop/Resume; a worker/session row cannot be interrupted there. Failed poll shows retry, not a stale success claim.
automate_and_routing.routing_contract: routing_roster is model tiers, not agent identities. It resolves configured then derived models and returns unavailable when neither exists. list_workers separately probes agent.yaml personas and excludes Pending engines from effective availability; goal dispatch checks the worker and rejects unavailable tier/pin rather than silently substituting.

computer_use.app_navigation: navigate_app/app_action/open_item emit app events and explicitly say screen delivery is unconfirmed; phone/watch voice origins are blocked. World place sections are limited to six compact habitats; desk tabs are UI-only.
computer_use.app_observation: observe_app reads bounded structured data on 20 surfaces; World observation reads agent.yaml dispatch personas and availability, not the 12 World characters or camera/job proof.
computer_use.browser: Browser tools can open the embedded Build browser, read its open tab, fetch public pages server-side, snapshot refs and click/type/select. The embedded bridge needs a desktop app; read_webpage refuses private/loopback hosts. An act requires a bound per-session snapshot identity and should re-snapshot afterward.
computer_use.desktop: Native control is macOS AX only, default disabled twice (extension and DESKTOP_CONTROL_ENABLED), and also needs Accessibility trust. It exposes status/apps/tree/click/type by ref; no screenshots, pixel actions, keyboard shortcuts, scrolling, launch of arbitrary apps or generalized OS workflow are implemented in this extension. Secure fields are refused and action tools are permission annotated.

findings.finding: World has Forecaster, Council and Grower characters whose background-worker ids exist in /api/agents, but worldAgentIds maps only the older five. World cannot offer their Manage Agent link and Settings cannot offer Open in World for them. Polybot and Picker also lack mappings, but neither has an Agents background descriptor, so an honest no-link status is correct there.
findings.resolution: Mapping and tests updated in current worktree; test execution and runtime navigation remain UNVERIFIED.

findings.finding: The agent-facing observe_app world result is only agent.yaml personas and probes. It cannot answer which World character is actually active, nor see several visible characters that are not dispatch personas. Its prose calls this the World-view worker roster, which risks overclaiming if the assistant answers a World-status request from it alone.

Reader and Watcher ambient states are simulated; Polybot is static. Daemon-wired World seats initialize idle and later apply events. The desk states that presence alone does not confirm a connection or running job; acceptance must check a task receipt or backing store before reporting work done.

Asking a named World specialist sends context into the shared orchestrator session. It does not directly call that worker, so a successful send is not specialist execution. The UI correctly says this; end-to-end acceptance must test follow-through and evidence separately.

Desktop Control cannot fulfill generic screenshot/coordinate/scroll/shortcut/launch workflows, and is disabled by default. Those tasks need a truthful unsupported or blocked result rather than a claim of full computer use.
